title: Galaxy NGC 1427A Plunges Toward the Fornax Galaxy Cluster
caption: The irregular galaxy NGC 1427A, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 1427A · constellation Fornax · about roughly 62 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA); Acknowledgment: M. Gregg (Univ. Calif.-Davis and Inst. for Geophysics and Planetary Physics, Lawrence Livermore Natl. Lab.)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: A small, bluish galaxy shaped roughly like an arrowhead is sprinkled with hot blue stars, while a yellower spiral sits to its upper left. The bluish one is NGC 1427A, an irregular galaxy about 62 million light-years away toward the constellation Fornax, and it is falling headlong into the Fornax galaxy cluster at 600 kilometers per second, nearly 400 miles per second.

Gas fills the space between the cluster's galaxies. As NGC 1427A plows through it, the galaxy's own gas is squeezed until it starts collapsing under its own gravity, setting off the widespread star birth that gives the galaxy its arrowhead outline. That shape seems to point along its direction of travel. Tidal pull from nearby cluster galaxies may also help trigger star formation on this scale.

The galaxy will not last. Within the next billion years it is expected to be torn apart, scattering its stars and leftover gas into the space between the cluster's members. Such disruptions are thought to have been very common early in the universe's history.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took the image, with F475W shown in blue, F625W and F775W in green, and F660N plus the near-infrared F850LP in red.
understand.eye: Part of the red channel is near-infrared light the eye cannot see, and 2.4 hours of exposure reveal galaxies far fainter than an eye could detect.

behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The spiral to the upper left only happens to lie near the same line of sight. It is some 25 times farther away and resembles our Milky Way, with stars forming in its symmetrical arms, but it has fewer very young stars and so looks yellower. More distant galaxies of many shapes and colors are scattered across the rest of the frame.
sources: NASA release: The Impending Destruction of NGC 1427A
alt: A small bluish irregular galaxy dotted with blue stars, with a yellowish spiral galaxy to its upper left and more distant galaxies behind.
